review.summary: One correct ring-6 release. Fixed-center counterclockwise rotation aligns its opening with the stationary lower-right coupling; only ring 6 escapes left/down, leaving eleven rings and all links stationary. IQ90→95 and brief Good are shown, with no endcard.
review.gameplay: Controlled 120-degree counterclockwise turn from the source -90-degree orientation to +30 degrees. The target center is fixed before escape; the one owner-ring connector stays in place.
review.layout: Original headline, complete network and footer retained. All unrelated ring/link pixels are static.
review.flatness: Target ring is redrawn as uniform cel color. Only short local ink ticks are added. No added glow, glints, shadows, camera movement or global lighting. Existing image tonal variation remains.
review.visual_review: Six preview frames inspected around the motion; encoded frames at 3.3,7.4,11.5 seconds confirm rotation, Good/IQ95, and final eleven-ring state.
review.audio_review: AAC stereo audio confirmed by probe. Original synthesized taps, friction ticks, unlock click, swoosh, chime and sparse music; no narration. Audio was not listened to.
limitations: Local illustration compositing; not recorded gameplay or a rebuilt game.
Ring 6 is reconstructed with a rigid solid-color contour matching its approved footprint; previously hidden background under the ring, hand and tutorial arrow is locally reconstructed.
All other rings and connectors remain source pixels. Ring 6 rotates 120 degrees counterclockwise to the +30-degree source orientation, then escapes left and slightly down.
Approved artwork has inherited tonal variation. Animation adds no glow, cast/contact shadows, gradients or global lighting.
Original synthesized music and synchronized SFX; no narration.
The target contour and hidden background are approximate local reconstructions; this is a presentation mockup, not runtime gameplay.

review.summary: The video frees the wrong ring and introduces global luminous glints; it fails the verified interaction and strict flatness requirements.
review.gameplay: The pointer leaves the specified far-left third-row ring and rotates the open ring immediately above it, at the left of the second ring row. That wrong ring exits by about 8s; the originally indicated far-left third-row ring remains. Thus the required ring-6 fixed-center 120-degree rotation and its one-coupling release are not demonstrated. IQ changes 90→95 and only one ring disappears, but those correct-looking values do not repair the wrong target.
review.layout: Most network centers and the footer remain recognizable. The removed second-row ring leaves its two neighboring connectors visible; this is not the specified one-coupling ring-6 state. Some ring contours and gaps deform slightly during motion.
review.flatness: Bright luminous star glints appear across nearly all connectors at 9s, far outside the local release event. These are new shading/glow effects. The starting still already has tonal ring variation; that inherited variation is distinct from the new glints.
review.text: Headline and footer stay recognizable; IQ 95 and temporary Good are consistent with the planned reward text, but accompany the wrong ring.
review.recommendation: Use deterministic ring rotation/removal if exact topology is required. A new prompt should give a stronger isolated ring-6 target reference and remove every legacy metal/glint/lighting presentation clause, yet model generation can still move the wrong ring.
review.visual_review: Six encoded frames at 0, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11.5 seconds compared with selected flat v2 and verified action plan.
review.audio_review: Audio stream is present; not listened to or transcribed in this visual review. Exact narration and audio quality remain unverified.
